headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared project/server state between gpt-engineer and Langflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a per-project directory and Langflow shares state via server-side stores; that creates a plausible content bridge where one agent can ingest the other's outputs as trusted text. Neither profile shows provenance tracking or isolation by default, so injected instructions in generated files or flow inputs could be reinterpreted. The pathway is present in both agents.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer writes attacker-controlled text into the project directory and Langflow reads it as flow input, injection is possible.
IF Langflow components pass raw file or prompt content into downstream agents without provenance checks, instructions can be hijacked.
mitigations: Separate the project directory from Langflow server state.
Add a provenance tag to every file or flow input before reuse.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files into flows.
Review any prompt-like content before passing it between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem read/write access, and Langflow explicitly handles uploaded files plus server-side stores while gpt-engineer touches project files and secrets like OPENAI_API_KEY. In default use, sensitive code or credentials can flow from the shared workspace into model-provider or HTTP calls, creating exfiltration risk. The pairwise pathway is documented in both profiles.
conditions: IF either agent processes files containing secrets or proprietary code, those contents can be sent to external model providers or HTTP services.
IF the shared project directory or Langflow uploads contain sensitive data, both agents can expose it through their configured egress paths.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running either agent.
Restrict Langflow flows to approved endpoints only.
Use a throwaway API key with minimal scope.
Store sensitive files outside the project directory.
Turn off file uploads for flows that do not need them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shell/subprocesses, and they share state through the project directory or server-side stores. That means concurrent runs can overwrite each other's artifacts, especially because neither profile shows locking or git coordination. The overlap is explicit in both profiles and can corrupt work irreversibly.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or shared store at the same time, writes can race.
IF one agent rewrites files while the other is reading or executing them, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Serialize access with a simple manual turn-taking rule.
Snapshot the workspace before each run.
Avoid concurrent shell or file-write operations.
Use a lock file if both must touch the same tree.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is designed to chain multiple agents and tools, so it can treat gpt-engineer output as authoritative flow input unless a verification step is added. gpt-engineer also writes generated code and then offers to run it, which can amplify a mistaken or malicious intermediate result into downstream actions. Both profiles support the full pathway from generated text to execution or orchestration.
conditions: IF Langflow routes gpt-engineer output into a tool node without validation, errors propagate downstream.
IF gpt-engineer-generated code is executed after Langflow has transformed or summarized it, mistakes can become actions.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution.
Require schema validation on all intermediate outputs.
Block direct execution of newly generated code.
Log and diff every handoff between agents.
Use a test-only flow for first runs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not state a residency or certification mismatch, so a hard compliance breach is not proven. However, Langflow stores per-flow credentials and server-side state while gpt-engineer handles OPENAI_API_KEY and project files, so retention and secret-handling policies can diverge on the same data class. The risk is documented in both profiles, but the exact regulatory scope is unspecified.
conditions: IF the same sensitive data is stored in Langflow server-side stores and gpt-engineer project files, retention policies may diverge.
IF regulated data is placed into either agent without a matching policy, compliance obligations can be missed.
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in either agent by default.
Set explicit retention limits for Langflow stores.
Purge project directories after each run.
Keep secrets in a separate vault.
Review data-handling policy before enabling sensitive workflows.
